evidence.note: CONFIRMED: a baseline-red comparison over failure text truncated to flakes.LINE_CHARS (240) treats two different ratchet causes behind the same visible prefix as the same failure. Regression test test_a_new_cause_hidden_by_a_truncated_failure_text_is_not_baseline_red fails on unfixed code (outcome='partial' baseline-red) and passes after _differs fails-safe on a truncated equality (outcome='failed' new offender).

A bug is not closed without a regression test that fails on the unfixed code (documented in the fix task): added one and watched it fail then pass. A tool that could not run is unavailable, never passed: reviewers/tests are run via their gates. Commit message states the mechanism; no forbidden trailers.
baseline_red._differs now fails safe on a truncated equality: _tally routes the id to 'different' (new offender) so a hidden cause is never read as baseline-red. Regression test covers it.

chunk_findings.detail: An identical, untruncated failure text whose length is exactly `LINE_CHARS` is now classified as a different failure. For example, if `LINE_CHARS == 80` and both the base and branch store `failed_reasons[ID] == "x" * 80` because the real test message is exactly 80 characters long, the previous text is not truncated at all and the cause is the same; the new line still returns `True`, so the gate moves the test into `different`/`new_failures` and reports a regression that does not exist. The method cannot distinguish a truncated-full prefix from an exact whole text, so the “whole text” promise in the docstring is not actually kept; it needs an explicit truncated marker or a digest/full-text comparison.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:144 (`return len(base) >= LINE_CHARS or len(branch) >= LINE_CHARS`)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:144 (`return len(base) >= LINE_CHARS or len(branch) >= LINE_CHARS`)

chunk_findings.detail: Given that `branch == base` (both are non-empty strings of length equal to `LINE_CHARS`), the code returns `True` (indicating a different failure/new offender). However, if `branch == base`, it means the truncated failure text on the branch is *identical* to the base, not different. Therefore, when the failure texts are completely identical up to the cut-off point, the code incorrectly flags it as a *different* failure (`True`), whereas identical failure texts should be recognized as the same failure to correctly preserve baseline-red status.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:143

chunk_findings.detail: Equal stored reasons are treated as a new cause whenever either string is at least `LINE_CHARS` long, but a cut of `text[:LINE_CHARS]` also yields that length when the full message is exactly `LINE_CHARS` and was not cut. Given base and branch both `"ratchet: found grew past:" + "x" * (LINE_CHARS - len("ratchet: found grew past:"))` (same site, whole text, `len == LINE_CHARS`), the new `return len(base) >= LINE_CHARS or len(branch) >= LINE_CHARS` is True, so the failure is not baseline-red. The same input is what the new test asserts as `different` / `new_failures`, so an unchanged ratchet that merely fills the cap is failed as a branch regression.

chunk_findings.detail: The two signature readers disagree on representation for legacy evidence. A base record produced by the previous flakes.py has only the capped `failed_reasons` text, so `_base_signatures` returns, for test `t`, the display string `"ratchet: found grew past: 30 allowed"`. The branch's new evidence has `failed_reason_hashes`, so `_failure_sigs` returns `content_digest("ratchet: found grew past: 30 allowed")` for the same `t`. `_differs` then computes `branch != base` and reports a new offender for an unchanged failure. This will false-positive against every base record that predates `failed_reason_hashes`, not just truncated/unknown-text cases.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_failure_sigs / _base_signatures

chunk_findings.detail: `failed_reason_hashes` is only populated for `kept` entries with `f["kind"] == "FAILED"`. Reasons added from `errored` (line 164-166 in flakes.py) are present in `failed_reasons` but are never assigned a digest. Because `_failure_sigs` does `ev.get("failed_reason_hashes") or ev.get("failed_reasons")`, one non-empty hash dict makes it discard every `failed_reasons` entry that lacks a hash. Concrete input: base is already red for `test_x` from an old setup error; branch changes that `test_x` to a new setup error while some other test yields `failed_reason_hashes = {"other": digest(...)}`. `_failure_sigs(branch)` omits `test_x`, so `_differs` sees branch missing for `test_x` and returns `False`; the new cause in the already-red `test_x` is hidden. This is the original B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause for non-FAILED reasons.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/flakes.py:139 (_failed_reason_hashes) and ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:141

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test hand-populates `ev["failed_reason_hashes"]` from the full branch/base reasons and never exercises the changed `ddflow/services/flakes.py` path that is supposed to emit that field. If flakes.py instead records a hash of the truncated display text (`branch_full[:LINE_CHARS]` and `base_full[:LINE_CHARS]`), the branch and base hashes are identical because the prefixes are identical; `GB.apply` then classifies `ID` as baseline-red and the original bug still happens in real CI, while this test still passes because it supplied the differing full-text hashes itself.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py:test_a_new_cause_hidden_by_a_truncated_failure_text_is_not_baseline_red

chunk_findings.detail: `_failure_sigs` and `_base_signatures` pick `failed_reason_hashes` or `failed_reasons` for the whole map, then `_differs` compares those strings with `!=`. A cached base that only has display text (the "old record" the new docstring allows) against a branch that has digests never matches: given base `failed_reasons[ID] == "x" * LINE_CHARS` and no hashes, and branch `failed_reasons[ID] == "x" * LINE_CHARS` plus `failed_reason_hashes[ID] == content_digest("x" * LINE_CHARS + "same cause")`, the gate treats an unchanged failure as `different` / `new_failures`. The same all-or-nothing choice drops any id that is only in `failed_reasons` once any hash exists, so an ERROR (or any unhashed id) whose text actually changed stays baseline-red.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_failure_sigs

chunk_findings.detail: Parse used to cap every pytest FAILED and ERROR reason at `LINE_CHARS` before it was stored. Truncation was removed there and put back only on the FAILED branch of `_error_fields` (`why[:LINE_CHARS]`), while `errored` is still stored with `reasons.setdefault(tid, why)` and hashes are built only for `kind == "FAILED"`. An ERROR line whose `why` is a multi-megabyte traceback is now written in full into committed `failed_reasons`. That same id is also absent from `failed_reason_hashes`, so once any FAILED hash is present the baseline gate ignores its text entirely.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/flakes.py:79

chunk_findings.detail: `failed_reason_hashes` is built only from `kept` rows where `f["why"]` is truthy. But `_error_fields` still supplies a reason from the failure tail when `f["why"]` is empty (`why = f["why"] or (_last_error_line(section[1]) if section else "")`) and then stores that reason in `failed_reasons`. Concrete input: parse a `FAILED t` / `ERROR t` line with no inline `why`; on the branch the tail line is `"x"*LINE_CHARS + "-branch-only-new-cause"` and on base it is `"x"*LINE_CHARS + "-base-old-cause"`. Both produce `failed_reasons["t"] == "x"*LINE_CHARS`, but because `f["why"]` is empty in both, `t` is absent from `failed_reason_hashes`. The gate then sees identical capped text and no digest for `t`, so it classifies the branch's new cause as pre-existing baseline red. This is the same defect as previous finding #2 for tail-recovered reason rows, and the probe “hashes cover FAILED+ERROR rows” does not answer it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/flakes.py:140 (with _error_fields at 159-165)

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard `if _is_digest(branch) != _is_digest(base): return False` makes the function return `False` whenever the base side is a legacy capped display text and the branch side is a full-reason digest. That is exactly the motivating legacy cache shape: `onbase[test_id] == "ratchet: found grew past: 30 allowed"` with no `failed_reason_hashes`, while `before[test_id] == content_digest("ratchet: found grew past: 31 allowed")`. `_is_digest(branch)` is true, `_is_digest(base)` is false, so `_differs` returns `False` and the gate still records the test as baseline-red, hiding the branch-added site. The change therefore fails to fix B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause for any baseline produced by the previous flakes.py, including the cited `fix-B-main-red-grok-harness-row` case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_differs

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_digest` classifies every 64-character lowercase hex string as a `content_digest` output, on the assumption that capped display text is prose. A legacy text-only reason whose display text is exactly 64 lowercase hex characters defeats that assumption. Concrete input: `base = {"t": "a" * 64}` and `branch = {"t": content_digest("a" * 64)}`; `_is_digest` is true for both, but the strings differ, so `_differs` returns `True` for an unchanged cause and falsely reports a new offender.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_is_digest

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not exercise the changed `ddflow/services/flakes.py` path that is supposed to emit `failed_reason_hashes`. It hand-populates `ev["failed_reason_hashes"]` from the full branch/base reasons directly. If `flakes.py` instead recorded `content_digest(branch_full[:LINE_CHARS])` and `content_digest(base_full[:LINE_CHARS])`, those digests would be identical because the visible prefixes are identical, so real CI would still classify the branch as baseline-red and hide the new cause; this test would still pass because it never runs the flakes parser/emitter. The test should drive the real flakes output through `GB.apply` or directly assert the emitter hashes the full reason.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py:test_a_new_cause_hidden_by_a_truncated_failure_text_is_not_baseline_red

chunk_findings.detail: `_failure_sigs` and `_base_signatures` return the hash map whenever it is non-empty, and `_differs` then treats any digest-vs-text pair as “same cause”. That hides a new cause that is already visible in the capped display text the branch still stores. Given a legacy base `failed_reasons["t"] == "ratchet: found grew past: 30 allowed"` (no hashes) and a branch `failed_reasons["t"] == "ratchet: found grew past: 99 allowed"` plus `failed_reason_hashes["t"] == content_digest(...)`, `_is_digest` differs so `_differs` returns False and the id stays baseline-red. That is the current CI cache shape for B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause: the counts differ inside `LINE_CHARS`, but the short-circuit never compares the two `failed_reasons` strings.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_differs

chunk_findings.detail: Hashes are still only built for `kept` rows with a truthy `f["why"]`, while an ERROR whose inline reason is empty still lands in `failed_reasons` via `_last_error_line`. `_failure_sigs` does `failed_reason_hashes or failed_reasons`, so one hashed FAILED row drops every unhashed id. Given base already red on `test_x` with reason `"ImportError: old"`, and a branch whose `kept` is `[{id: test_x, kind: ERROR, why: ""}, {id: test_a, kind: FAILED, why: "assert 1"}]` with the tail line now `"ImportError: new"`, the branch signature map has only `test_a`, `_differs("test_x")` sees no branch text and returns False, and the new setup error stays baseline-red.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/flakes.py:_failed_reason_hashes

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier probe still does not answer the vacuous-test defect: this function still builds `failed_reason_hashes` itself with `content_digest(branch_full)` / `content_digest(base_full)` and never runs the `flakes.py` parser that CI actually uses to fill that field. Given pytest output whose failure text is `"x" * LINE_CHARS + "branch grew ..."` on the branch and `"x" * LINE_CHARS + "the base is red..."` on the base, a parser that hashes `why[:LINE_CHARS]` (identical prefixes) makes `GB.apply` treat `ID` as baseline-red, while this test still passes because it injects digests of the uncut strings. The claimed FAILED+ERROR hash coverage is therefore unenforced by the regression test that is supposed to close B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_baseline_red.py:test_a_new_cause_hidden_by_a_truncated_failure_text_is_not_baseline_red

chunk_findings.detail: `_failure_sigs` and `_base_signatures` return the hash map whenever it is non-empty, and `_differs` then treats any digest-vs-text pair as “same cause”. That hides a new cause that is already visible in the capped display text the branch still stores. Given a legacy base `failed_reasons["t"] == "ratchet: found grew past: 30 allowed"` (no hashes) and a branch `failed_reasons["t"] == "ratchet: found grew past: 99 allowed"` plus `failed_reason_hashes["t"] == content_digest(...)`, `_is_digest` differs so `_differs` returns False and the id stays baseline-red. That is the current CI cache shape for B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause: the counts differ inside `LINE_CHARS`, but the short-circuit never compares the two `failed_reasons` strings.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_differs

chunk_findings.detail: Hashes are still only built for `kept` rows with a truthy `f["why"]`, while an ERROR whose inline reason is empty still lands in `failed_reasons` via `_last_error_line`. `_failure_sigs` does `failed_reason_hashes or failed_reasons`, so one hashed FAILED row drops every unhashed id. Given base already red on `test_x` with reason `"ImportError: old"`, and a branch whose `kept` is `[{id: test_x, kind: ERROR, why: ""}, {id: test_a, kind: FAILED, why: "assert 1"}]` with the tail line now `"ImportError: new"`, the branch signature map has only `test_a`, `_differs("test_x")` sees no branch text and returns False, and the new setup error stays baseline-red.

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier probe still does not answer the vacuous-test defect: this function still builds `failed_reason_hashes` itself with `content_digest(branch_full)` / `content_digest(base_full)` and never runs the `flakes.py` parser that CI actually uses to fill that field. Given pytest output whose failure text is `"x" * LINE_CHARS + "branch grew ..."` on the branch and `"x" * LINE_CHARS + "the base is red..."` on the base, a parser that hashes `why[:LINE_CHARS]` (identical prefixes) makes `GB.apply` treat `ID` as baseline-red, while this test still passes because it injects digests of the uncut strings. The claimed FAILED+ERROR hash coverage is therefore unenforced by the regression test that is supposed to close B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause.

chunk_findings.detail: The new comparison breaks against base evidence recorded by the pre-change `flakes.py`. Before this change, `flakes.py` stored pytest failure reasons via `seen.setdefault(..., (m["why"] or "")[:LINE_CHARS])`, so a cached base record for an already-red test contains the reason truncated to `LINE_CHARS`. The branch now stores the full reason. Given an unchanged failure whose summary is `"x" * LINE_CHARS + " - same cause"`, `before[t]` is the full string while `onbase[t]` is only the `"x" * LINE_CHARS` prefix; `_differs` computes `branch != base` as true and reports `t` as a new offender even though the base and branch failed for the identical cause. This will falsely flag long-running pre-existing red tests on first use after this change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_differs

chunk_findings.detail: The new full-text comparison in `_differs` cannot recognize a legacy baseline cache entry written by the pre-fix code, where `failed_reasons[ID]` was stored truncated to `LINE_CHARS`. Given an already-red test whose cached base reason is `"ratchet grew:" + "x"*LINE_CHARS` and whose branch reason is now stored whole as `"ratchet grew:" + "x"*LINE_CHARS + "clients.py"` (the base's untruncated cause is also `clients.py`; only retention changed), the two strings differ, so `_differs` returns `True` and the gate moves the ID into `different`/`new_failures` instead of `still_failing`—a false new failure. The added regression test does not catch this because its `run` mock returns a whole `base_full` (`"... + "hookio.py"`), never the legacy truncated cache entry that still exists in pre-fix baselines.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/baseline_red.py:_differs

chunk_findings.detail: `_differs` treats any string inequality as a new cause, but a base measured before this change still has the old `[:LINE_CHARS]` cap while the branch now stores the summary whole. Given a cached base reason `"ratchet grew:" + "x" * (LINE_CHARS - len("ratchet grew:"))` that was the cut of the same message the branch now stores as that prefix plus `"hookio.py"`, `branch != base` is true even though the cause did not change, so `on_base` reports a new offender and the gate fails an unchanged already-red test until that truncated cache entry is gone. A shared prefix of length `LINE_CHARS` is exactly the ambiguous legacy shape; failing closed here is still the wrong verdict for an identical continuation.
